In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the positive excursion of the δ13C isotope curve in the Prague Basin was caused by the combination of the following factors: (a) a sea-level fall, (b) a reduced sedimentation of cephalopod limestones, (c) a reduced sediment input from shallow-water settings and (d) a strong increase in the productivity of the organic carbon.
the Lau Event is recorded in the Prague Basin with a positive shift in δ13C values.
the δ13C excursion in the Prague Basin is caused by a sea level fall, which was accompanied by a strong reduction of sedimentation in shallow parts of the Prague Basin.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Lau Event is well documented in the Prague Basin, but the maximum of the excursion is not recorded in the shallow parts due to the sea-level fall.
a sea-level fall and a subsequent sea-level rise were the main factors controlling the sedimentation and the δ13C signal of the Kopaninas.
the Lau Event was recorded in the Prague Basin in a more pronounced form compared with the Muslovka and the Požary quarrie sections.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Prague Basin was not affected by a major drop in sea level, but instead experienced a significant positive excursion in δ13C values.

the Prague Basin is a suitable area for the reconstruction of the global carbon cycle in the late Silurien, because of the high quality of the sections, the presence of different depositional settings and the absence of significant stratigraphical gaps.
the Prague Basin, as a middle palaeo-latitude basin, is a good analogue for palaeo-latitudinal reconstructions of other peri-Gondwanan basins, which were situated in similar latitudes.
